result.unit: ch6 ending and end screen (15:45-16:51), 945.00-1010.96 s, module ch6
result.summary: Overall this unit is in good shape, and every planned beat renders and lands on time. Measured against timing.json: the counter rolls at 948.43 on 'tenth', the Explorer faints at 952.65 on 'Reminder', the tiles fold into the filmstrip at 955.93 on 'wins', the tear comes at 958.07 on 'torn', the arcs start at 961.77 on 'been', 1620 lands at 964.06 on 'ago', the underline starts at 968.49 on 'accident' and glows gold at 970.23 on 'right', the snap hits at 973.00 on 'breakup', the today frame lights up at 976.89 on 'frame', the live hole opens at 982.12 on 'shot', the Afar dot shows at 983.23, the Y draws at 984.59 on 'cracks', the south arm pulses and creeps at 988.91 on 'East', the next-video tile appears at 993.91 on 'next' and the subscribe ring at 997.39 on 'subscribe'. I scanned all 1979 frames at 30 fps for brightness and frame-to-frame change: there are no black frames, colour flashes or single-frame glitches. The only dark moment is a planned 0.25 s fade into the Bacon desk at 963.03. Pacing is dense, with a cut or mode change every 2-5 s. Both gags read: the faint, and the waving Explorer with the porch light. The bookend globe matches the cold-open frame at t=1. End screen: the tile placeholder is at x1010-1810, y240-690 and the subscribe ring is at (1110,830) with radius 74, all above the bottom 12 %. The right side is darkened and the title sits above the tile. The only things under the reserved areas are the Somali coast and the last ~50 px of the Gulf of Aden arm, and the YouTube element will cover both. The final frame (1010.933) is the end card, not black. The final frames are not fully static: sparks, the light running round the tile border and the subscribe pulse keep moving. The globe background behind them, however, freezes for the last ~4 s (issue 2). Three defects remain: the gold 'cidit' underline hangs off the edge of the page photo (major), the end-screen background freezes (minor), and the assembled Gondwana is on screen only ~0.1 s before it snaps apart (minor). NOTE FOR ALL REVIEWERS: the contact-sheet labels from review_frames.py are 0.467 s early. Its ffmpeg fps=1 filter (round=near) outputs input frame 14 of each second, so 't_0963.00.jpg' actually shows t=963.467. I checked this against exact frames: mean difference 4.0 at 963.467 versus 33.8 at 963.000. Make sync calls from exact seeks, or fix the tool by using fps=1:round=down or labelling frames t=15*i+k+14/30.

issues.segment: s106 (Bacon page callback, 'Looks like he was right. It wasn't an accident.')
issues.problem: While the 'right' underline glows gold, the second half of the phrase ('quod non temere ac-' / 'cidit.') is cropped and its underline sticks out past the left edge of the page photo. The Ken Burns push-in shoves 'cidit.' past the photo edge, so it reads 'idit.' and then 'dit.'. Its underline hangs ~40-50 px past the photo onto the paper border and dark desk. A glowing stroke floating outside the page looks like a render error, right on the beat that is supposed to point at the quote.
issues.evidence: Exact frames: x_972.2.png shows the gold underline running x~280-410 while the page photo starts at x~318-330, and the word reads 'dit.'. x_970.9.png shows the underline starting at x~300-314 with the word reading 'idit.'. x_969.3.png shows the same underline still fully inside the page (x~350-465). The printKB maps the underline start (u=0.075) to x=354 at 968.45, x=330 at 970.23 and x=283 at 972.97: the end zoom of 1.36 makes the visible slice of the page too narrow for this line of text, which needs at most ~1.30.
issues.fix: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js, s106 page shot base(PG0, PG1): in L.printKB(ctx, img('p246'), prog(t, PG0, PG1), [330, 70, 1260, 700], [0.46, 0.142, 1.25], [0.47, 0.146, 1.36], ...) change the end framing to [0.454, 0.146, 1.28]. Computed result: the 'cidit' underline starts at x~349 and the 'quod...ac-' underline ends at x~1571, so both stay inside the 330-1590 window for the whole move. As a safety net, wrap the L.highlight/L.underline calls in ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(330, 70, 1260, 700); ctx.clip(); ... ctx.restore();

issues.problem: The end-screen background (the held Afar globe still) drifts to a dead stop about 4 s before the hard cut. In the final seconds only the 16 px sparks on the rift, the light running round the tile border and the subscribe pulse move. The plan asks for 'visuals keep moving to the final frame'. Cause: a double ease. const k = E.inOutSine(prog(t, AFH, END)) applies prog's default cubic inOut and then inOutSine on top, so k = 0.971 at 1005.3 s and 0.9975 at 1007.2 s.
issues.evidence: An 8x-amplified difference between exact frames x_1008.0.png and x_1010.933.png shows zero change anywhere in the globe image; only the sparks, the border light and the subscribe ring and pill differ. Mean frame-to-frame difference (64x36 scale) falls from 0.31 (998.5-1002 s) to 0.12 (1008-1009.5 s) and 0.10 (1009.5-1010.9 s). The mean difference over the left background area is 0.88 between 1008.0 and 1009.5, and 0.44 between 1009.5 and 1010.4.
issues.fix: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js, s108-s109 Afar/end-screen base(AF0, AF1): replace `const k = E.inOutSine(prog(t, AFH, END));` with `const k = prog(t, AFH, END, E.lin);`. Optionally make the move a little larger: zoomAbout(ctx, 1 + 0.10 * k, -60 * k, 24 * k). In drawRift use `const wide = 1.5 + 7 * prog(t, SEG('s109').start, END, E.lin);` so the drift and the rift widening carry through the last frame. The speed jump at AFH is only ~0.45 %/s, so it will not show.

issues.segment: s106 ('It was a breakup' Gondwana snap)
issues.problem: The assembled Gondwana (the callback to s073) is on screen for only 3 frames before the pieces start flying, and the snap flash is already on top of it. The breakup reads as a cut to an exploding globe rather than 'the supercontinent we saw earlier breaking up'. The page shot ends at M.breakup-0.08 and the snap is at M.breakup-0.05.
issues.evidence: Exact frames from 972.900 to 973.367 (snap_strip.png): the page is still up at 972.933. Gondwana appears at 972.967 with the impact flash already drawn, holds through 973.033, and is visibly separating by 973.067. By 973.367 the continents are near their present-day positions and the camera is diving to Antarctica.
issues.fix: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js, s106: change `const PG0 = CP1, PG1 = M.breakup - 0.08;` to `PG1 = M.breakup - 0.42`. GO0 = PG1 follows automatically and tSnap = M.breakup - 0.05 stays as it is. The still Gondwana then holds ~0.37 s on 'It was a...' and snaps on 'breakup'. The page keeps 970.23-972.63 for the gold underline and the 'NOT AN ACCIDENT.' headline.

result.unit: ch6 where the drip goes next, part 1 (14:35-15:45)
result.summary:
This unit is strong and well timed. The chapter card, the ridge glow and 1620 pill, the school bus in the magma gap, the time scrub to +250, the spin and fog with four '?' marks, the 2x2 grid, the counters and pills, the neighbor gag (Run_Left, Run_Right, Idle, then the comment bubble), the splash and the Tuesday card all land within 0.15 s of their marker words. Proxima (coast to coast on 'Africa', counter landing on +250) and Amasia read clearly.

The problems are two plate-geometry errors in the hand-keyed future models:
1. Blocker: Aurica cuts New Guinea along the 141E border and draws Indonesian Papua on top of Australia's Top End, right inside the 'middle' glow ring.
2. Major: Novopangaea moves Antarctica's centre to sit under Cape Horn, so all of Patagonia lies on top of the ice sheet.

Each is a one-line fix: the plate assignment in ch6_future.js plateOf(), and the AN target in ch6.js MODELS[1]. Both stills come back in the grid and corner tiles until 937.9.

There are three minor items:
- The Novopangaea hold is frozen for about 3.2 s.
- The tiny planet's edge covers the bottom corner tiles in gag 10a.
- The US tracker dot is clipped at the top of the frame and sits on the Aurica pill.

The Explorer is lit, nothing important is in the bottom 12%, and there are no colour flashes. The two 0.3 s fades up from black at 937.88 and 943.88 are deliberate fadeIn transitions and land in narration pauses.

Note for other reviewers: review_frames.py contact-sheet labels are 0.5/fps early. A 1 fps sheet frame labelled T is really T+0.5 s (checked by pixel match against the exact frame at 893.5). Every time in this report comes from exact frames.

Evidence files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/x1_ch6a/x/ (x_928.3.jpg, crop_aus_928.jpg, x_909.5.jpg, x_934.5.jpg, x_936.3.jpg). The plate-math check is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/research/review/w3/x1_ch6a/tools/plates.py.

issues.problem: In the Aurica hero shot, New Guinea is cut along the straight 141E Indonesia/PNG border. Indonesian Papua stays on the Eurasia plate, swings 24 deg east with it, and is drawn on top of Australia's Top End and Kimberley as a dark-green block with a ruler-straight east edge. It sits at the edge of the yellow 'middle' glow ring on the focal continent. Papua New Guinea floats north of Australia with its own ruler-straight west edge. The broken still is also used for the Aurica grid and corner tile until 937.9.
issues.evidence: Exact frames 924.0, 924.9, 926.0 and 928.3. In x_928.3.jpg (crop_aus_928.jpg) a dark-green block sits on Australia's north coast at about x 620-720, y 430-545 with a vertical straight edge, and the PNG fragment at about x 715-845, y 320-385 has a straight west edge. Plate math with the module's quaternions: EU qPole(90,0,24) puts Sorong at -0.9/155.3 and Merauke at -8.5/164.4, while AU qMove([-25,134],[-15,167],12) puts Darwin at -4.6/159.1 and Gove at -2.2/164.4, so Papua lands on the Top End. The future shader composites plates first-wins in the order NA, SA, AF, EU, AU, AN, so EU covers AU.
issues.fix: ch6_future.js plateOf(): as the first line after `const name = ...` add `if (name === 'Indonesia' && lo > 130.5 && la < -0.5) return 'AU';` so western New Guinea, Aru and Tanimbar move with the Australian plate (which is also where they are geologically). Checked with the same maths: Papua then lands at 2.6-8.3N, 155-166E, joined to PNG (Wewak 8.4/167.5, Daru 3.0/169.1) and north of the moved Top End, with no overlap. Seram and Halmahera stay on EU. Re-render chunks 61-62 and any later chunk that shows the Aurica still (s105 filmstrip).

issues.problem: The Novopangaea 'contact' is really an overlap: South America's whole southern cone is drawn on top of Antarctica. Antarctica's centre (the South Pole) is moved to sit exactly under Cape Horn, so Patagonia runs about 190 px into the middle of the cream ice sheet, with the Antarctic Peninsula wrapped around it like a hand. It is on screen full-frame for 5 s while 'the Americas hit Antarctica first' plays, then stays in the cyan tile until 937.9.
issues.evidence: Exact frame 909.5 (x_909.5.jpg): the South America tip runs from about (850-990, 640) down to Cape Horn at about (870, 830), inside the cream Antarctica, which spans about x 650-1130, y 620-1000. Plate math: AN qMove([-90,0],[-56,-118]) puts the pole at -56.0/-118.0 and Cape Horn on the SA plate lands at -56.8/-116.8. A point-in-polygon test puts all 1,990 Chile and Argentina coastline vertices south of 40S inside the moved Antarctica.
issues.fix: ch6.js MODELS[1].plates.AN: change qMove([-90, 0], [-56, -118]) to qMove([-90, 0], [-72, -117]). Tested: only 43 Tierra del Fuego vertices then overlap, which reads as a crash; [-73,-117] gives zero overlap. Change contact.ll from [-45, -75] to [-55.5, -67.5] so the impact ring fires at Cape Horn. Optionally move the last camera key from lat -32 to -38 so the ice sheet stays in frame.

issues.problem: After the NOVOPANGAEA pill pops in (908.18), the picture is in effect frozen until the tile shrinks at 911.59: a pre-rendered hold frame with only a 3.5% push-in. Nothing happens during 'One team's favorite bet', about 3.2 s of static frame.
issues.evidence: Downscaled exact frames: the total mean absolute change from 908.4 to 911.4 is 5.2/255, and from 910.8 to 911.4 it is 0.12/255.
issues.fix: ch6.js MODELS[1]: change tShrink from s101 - 0.5 to s101 - 1.3, so the tile flies back into the grid on 'favorite bet' (about 910.8). Alternatively, give MODELS[1] an extra() that fires L.yRing at the rotated contact point at wf('s100','favorite').

issues.problem: In gag 10a the 3D stage (the tiny planet) is drawn after the corner tiles, so the planet's edge and glow cut across the inner bottom corners of the Amasia and Aurica tiles. At 936.3 about a third of the Amasia still, including its US dot, is hidden behind the planet, and the edge glow crosses the Aurica tile.
issues.evidence: Exact frames 934.5 and 936.3: the planet edge crosses the Aurica tile from about (1365,785) to (1550,893) and the Amasia tile from about (330,893) to (556,800).
issues.fix: ch6.js CORNER (line ~465): raise the bottom row from y 636 to y 520. The tiles then end at 777, clear of the planet edge, and the Explorer is still drawn in front of them.

issues.problem: The white US tracker dot sits on the top edge of the globe in Novopangaea and is half cut off by the frame top at about (854,15) for the whole beat, so it does its job of marking home poorly. In Aurica, the dot and its pulsing ring land on the top-right border of the AUSTRALIA + AMERICA pill at about (1110,70) from 926.2 to 928.8.
issues.fix: ch6.js drawUS(): after the projection add `const fa = clamp((q.y - 150) / 80); if (fa <= 0) return;` and multiply the dot and shadow alpha by fa. This also cleans the grid stills, which are rendered through drawLive/drawHold.
